source: General guidance based on WHO/UNICEF infant and young child feeding recommendations and WHO IMCI danger signs. Demo content for a student project: review with the Family Health Bureau before real use.

body.en: Give only breast milk, day and night, at least 8 times in 24 hours. No water, other milk or food is needed before 6 months.
Hold your baby close, smile and talk to her. Answer her sounds; this is how she learns to talk.
Put her to sleep on her back. Never leave her alone on a bed or near the hearth. Wash your hands before feeding.

Keep breastfeeding. From 6 months give thick mashed food 2–3 times a day; from 9 months 3–4 small meals, mashed or finely chopped, and 1–2 healthy snacks. Add an egg, fish, dhal or leafy greens to rice.
Name things around the house and play peek-a-boo. Let her hold a spoon and try to feed herself.
She is starting to crawl and pull up. Keep small objects, kerosene and medicines out of reach.
Give 3–4 meals of family food a day and 1–2 snacks such as fruit. Keep breastfeeding up to 2 years and beyond.
Read, sing and tell simple stories. Give her pots, spoons and blocks to play with.
Watch her near wells, buckets and ponds, and keep her away from hot pots and the hearth.

title.en: A mix of foods every day

body.en: Give 3 meals and 2 snacks of family food: rice or bread, dhal, fish or egg, vegetables and fruit. Keep sweets and sugary drinks for rare treats.
Count, draw and play outside together. Ask questions and listen to the answers.
Hold her hand near the road. Keep medicines, kerosene and sharp tools locked away.
Fits, fast or hard breathing, not able to drink or breastfeed, vomiting everything, or very sleepy and hard to wake: go to hospital now or call 1990.
Bleeding, a bad headache or blurred vision, fits, swelling of the face or hands, fever, water breaking, or the baby moving less: go to hospital now or call 1990.
